messages:
Sara: Quick kickoff — we need a concise PRD for the new quotas/rate-limit model. Main goals: per-tenant and per-route caps, separate metering for tokens vs embeddings, clear overage semantics, UI for change requests. Need acceptance criteria and edge cases.

Mike: +1. Three enterprise pilots asked for preserved burst windows and predictably billed bursts. Also want an API to request temporary increases (programmatic overrides).

Jordan: Streaming + function-calls complicate counting. We must define when tokens are considered billed (partial tokens mid-stream?). Also decide 429 vs queueing behavior.

Eva: Metering proposal: publish two counters — tokens_consumed and embedding_units. embedding_units = ceil(vectors * vector_size / bucket_size). Keep it simple for billing exports.

Nate: Ops flag: naive checks against central DB on each request will be a perf problem. Spec should require local token-bucket checks with eventual sync. Add SLA for mismatch rate.

Sara: First-pass acceptance criteria: 
- API: /v1/quotas GET/PUT with tenant, route, model granularity
- UI: Limits panel to request/increase with audit trail and expiry
- Billing: tokens_consumed + embedding_units in CSV + BigQuery exports
- Behavior: hard limit -> immediate 429; soft limit -> allow burst up to X% for Ys then 429
- Rollout: canary 5% -> 3 pilot tenants -> global
- Docs: migration guide + examples

Mike: Edge cases to call out: client disconnect during streaming, function-call expansions (tool returns long text), async/background jobs consuming tokens, cross-region failover counting.

Jordan: Heuristic idea: bill on token-commit (when runtime appends to output buffer). If disconnect before commit, do not count tokens for metering but we might still record compute usage for internal reconciliation. Refunds are tricky for invoices.

Eva: For billing semantics, recommend: invoice by tokens accepted by runtime. For aborted streams, create adjustment events and reconcile weekly for enterprise customers only. Public tiers get no refunds.

Nate: Implementation note: local leaky-bucket with check+reserve on runtime node; publish deltas to central ledger every N seconds. Acceptance must include <5% false accept/reject rate under target load.

Sara: API override example (proto):
```
POST /v1/quotas/tenants/{tenant_id}/overrides
{
  "route": "/v1/chat",
  "window_seconds": 60,
  "max_tokens": 120000,
  "reason": "pilot burst"
}
```

Mike: Must create audit log entry on override creation and expiration; TTL on overrides; RBAC: only account admins + SEs can create for enterprise.

Eva: UI flows: request increase -> auto-approve for dev/free tier up to threshold T, manual review above T. Show usage graph, reset time, forecasted spend.

Jordan: QA checklist: simulate traffic hitting both per-route and per-model caps, simulate region split to ensure no double-counting, validate embedding_units mapping across vector sizes.

Sara: Rollout timeline draft:
- Wk1: PRD + API proto
- Wk2-3: Metering + local bucket checks implementation
- Wk4: UI + audit logs + billing exports
- Wk5: Canary + pilot migrations
- Wk8: Full rollout + deprecate legacy caps

Nate: Migration approach: legacy-cap customers get 90-day opt-in; provide conversion tooling that maps legacy caps to per-route profiles and suggests burst rules.

Mike: Open decisions for PRD: default soft-burst % and duration; rounding rules for token vs embedding billing (ceil vs floor); refunds policy details; quota evaluation precedence when route + model caps apply.

Sara: Owners: API/infra -> Nate; billing/export -> Eva; UI/UX -> Mike; QA -> Jordan. I will draft the PRD and ping for reviews. Add missing edge cases here. :eyes:
